_: The five findings of the amethyst (Scoring) hero, in the house keys. Provenance: every figure in a/b is a cell of ~/Documents/cascade-scoring/releve-public.json at seal `sceau`; addresses in `source` ({table, palier, seuil, mesure}, optional `champ` naming which Rate field is displayed, or {table, compte}); re-verified mechanically at the displayed precision. Finding 01 states a deliberate design fact the record proves: geography scores zero on both sides because every written dossier resides in ordinary Union countries and no official country list was copied into the data, so risk lives in declared fields, not passports. Finding 04 shows the amethyst's reversal: here the generated variants are HARSHER than the written dossiers on the best factor, which is exactly why separation is a rule and not a convenience. `annotations` are provisional fractions of the shelving tray (eight bays, registry order, amethyst pile = recall bound, ivory pile = false alerts, brass shelf = floor): texts and fractions were measured against the delivered frames (rayonnage-reel/parchemin-01..05). One answer for the re-render: state 2 lights the tenure bay, but finding 02 is about PRODUCT: light bay three (the labels already anchor it, so they hold as-is once the light moves). State 4 keeps its own framing, the two-bay close-up.

findings.titre: Geography scores zero recall and zero false alerts here.
findings.phrase: Each file in the record resides in an ordinary Union country, because no official country list was copied into the data. The geography factor therefore scores 0% recall and 0% false alerts, and risk lives in the declared facts while the country plays no part.
findings.leg_a: recall 0% for the geography factor on 42 files, interval 0% to 8%
findings.leg_b: false alerts 0% on 42 files, interval 0% to 8%

findings.titre: The product factor reaches 92.9% recall at 23.8% false alerts.
findings.phrase: Scoring only the products a client holds reaches 92.9% recall, since correspondent accounts, private banking and crypto rails carry the signal. The same factor alerts on 23.8% of the retained files, and each one is a review.
findings.leg_a: recall 92.9% for the product factor at 0.50, interval 81% to 98%, 42 files
findings.leg_b: false alerts 23.8% on 42 files, interval 13% to 39%

findings.titre: No single factor reaches the 90% recall floor.
findings.phrase: The tool asks the lower bound of measured recall to reach 90%. On the 42 files no factor reaches it: the best lower bound is 81% for product, and behaviour, with no false alert, reaches only 52%. Scoring on more than one factor is needed.
findings.leg_a: highest recall lower bound, product at 0.50: 81%, interval 81% to 98%
findings.leg_b: cleanest factor, behaviour at 0.50: 52%, zero false alerts, interval 52% to 79%
annotations: recall floor 90%: unmet by any factor

findings.titre: The product factor scores 79.4% recall on variants against 92.9% on written files.
findings.phrase: The same cell scores 92.9% recall on 42 files, all written, and 79.4% on 126 files, all generated. Here the generated set is harder, and it is still measured on its own and kept out of the headline rate.
findings.leg_a: recall 92.9% for product at 0.50 on 42 files, interval 81% to 98%
findings.leg_b: recall 79.4% at the same cell on 126 files, interval 71% to 86%

findings.titre: The public record holds written files and generated variants.
findings.phrase: Each file behind these findings is in the public record: 42 files written, seven per typology, and 126 files generated under a seed. Two files from your systems, reviews and customer attributes, rerun the full grid at your desk.
findings.leg_a: written escalated files behind the measured rates, seven per typology
findings.leg_b: generated variants behind the separate rates, typologies preserved by construction
annotations: your files rerun at your desk
